repairs.action: Dropped, keeping the first occurrence of each fact_id
repairs.why: Duplicate rows double-count revenue and inflate every total
A blank is a missing observation; dropping the row would bias the mean

repairs.action: Set to missing, then imputed with the same median (698.8)
repairs.why: Impossible values are not observations and would drag any average down
A discount over 100% produces negative revenue and breaks the invoice check
Guessing an industry would invent data; naming it Unknown keeps the row honest

repairs.action: Assigned the most common region ("North America")
repairs.why: A broken foreign key makes rows vanish from any per-region total

repairs.why: Letting pandas guess can swap day and month, producing plausible wrong dates

repairs.defect: Rep hired after the customer signed up
repairs.why: There is no correct rep to assign; the honest fix is to mark it and exclude it

invoice_reconciliation.tolerance_note: Generator applies 3% invoice noise, so 5% is the correct tolerance

churn.caution: With 200 customers, most category differences fall inside the 95% confidence interval. Only categories flagged differs_from_overall should be described as a pattern.

mrr_identity.question: Can MRR be predicted?
mrr_identity.verdict: It is arithmetic, not a prediction problem
mrr_identity.formula: mrr = seats x list_price_per_seat x (1 - discount_pct)
mrr_identity.note: The R² is high because the right-hand side IS the invoice formula. This model has no predictive content and is reported only to show the difference between explaining a quantity and re-deriving it.

ols.question: What explains nps_score?
ols.formula: nps_score ~ usage_per_seat + support_tickets + discount_pct + seats + is_annual_contract + industry_risk + C(segment)
ols.interpretation: The model as a whole is highly significant, but only 1 of 8 terms is individually significant. The overall test and the individual tests answer different questions, and a variable can matter as part of a group while adding nothing on its own.

prediction.interpretation: Cross-validated R² on unseen customers. The spread across folds matters as much as the mean: with 200 customers a difference smaller than the fold-to-fold variation is not a real difference.

regression.tools_note: statsmodels is used for inference (coefficients, standard errors, p-values, confidence intervals). scikit-learn is used for prediction (out-of-sample performance under cross-validation). They answer different questions.

baseline.note: Predicting 'nobody churns' is 80% accurate and identifies no one. That is why accuracy is not the metric used below.

model_comparison.note: Cross-validated ROC-AUC. The AUC here is high partly because the data was generated by a logistic process using these very features — a well-specified model recovers it almost exactly. On real customer data, where the true process is unknown and includes factors nobody recorded, expect materially lower.

cost_assumptions.note: Illustrative figures. A retention team would supply the real ones.

threshold_analysis.scoring: Out-of-fold predictions from 5-fold cross-validation: every customer is scored by a model trained without them.
threshold_analysis.interpretation: With these costs the best cut-off is 0.20, not 0.50. It catches 95% of churners against 68% at the default, and lowers expected cost by $53,700 on this test set.

feature_importance.note: Importance is measured on held-out data by shuffling one column and re-scoring. A feature with a high importance but no true coefficient is one the model learned from noise.

marginal_versus_conditional.interpretation: The coefficient on discount is larger once usage, size and sentiment are held constant, which is the signature of a variable masked by correlated companions. BUT: on 200 customers neither estimate is significantly different from zero, so this is a direction of travel, not an established effect. Reporting the interval is the difference between noticing a pattern and claiming one.

classification.leakage_warning: Churn is derived from the panel (last observed month < final month). It is never a column on fact_subscription_monthly. churn_reason_id is post-hoc and must never be used as a feature.

density_based.interpretation: Density-based methods look for dense regions and are free to find none. DBSCAN found at most 1 cluster(s) across the whole eps sweep, and HDBSCAN classified 100% of customers as noise. Taken together they indicate a continuum rather than distinct groups.

stability.verdict: moderately stable — the broad shape holds, the edges move

alignment_with_known_segments.interpretation: If a cluster is dominated by one existing segment, the algorithm has recovered a label we already had. Only clusters that mix segments are telling us something new.

clustering.embedding_note: Only the variance explained is stored. The t-SNE and UMAP coordinates themselves are not written to the results file, because step 6 draws its charts in the browser from the customer table instead of displaying pre-rendered images.
clustering.verdict: KMeans returns k clusters whatever k you ask for. DBSCAN and HDBSCAN are free to find none, and did. The emergent two-group split is stable and separates small from large accounts, but it is a continuum cut in half rather than a discovery of distinct customer types.
